column1: # JSON SCHEMA EXPORT -- the bridge to every structured-output API.
# The review's finding I / SUPPORT.md act 2. Every major LLM provider's
# structured-output API constrains generation to JSON Schema and to
# nothing else, so without an export a model cannot ride that path and
# then be `vet`ted as the semantic gate -- and an MCP tool's
# `inputSchema`, which the protocol REQUIRES to be JSON Schema, cannot
# be derived from an aontu tool model at all.
# EVERY EXPECTATION HERE WAS OBTAINED BY RUNNING BOTH ENGINES AND
# DIFFING. The expect object is the schema AND the loss report, because
# a schema that silently DROPPED a construct would look identical to one
# that carried it -- and a dropped constraint makes the schema admit
# MORE than the model does, which is the failure this language exists to
# refuse. The CLI's envelope (version, verb) is not compared.
# WHAT CROSSES EXACTLY: kinds to types, concrete scalars to `const`, a
# disjunction of scalars to `enum` (and its preference to `default`),
# bounds to minimum/maximum with the OPEN endpoints as the exclusive
# keywords, `re` to `pattern` (aontu's portable subset is a subset of
# ECMA-262, which is what JSON Schema reads), `neq` to `not: {enum}`,
# uniqueItems, optional keys to an absence from `required`, and -- the
# one aontu and JSON Schema say identically -- `close()` to
# `additionalProperties: <template>`, which is what it means; a written
# list is a TUPLE, so prefixItems plus items:false.
# WHAT DOES NOT, AND IS REPORTED: an evaluate-only `must()` (opaque by
# construction), the exact `0d` leaves (JSON has one number type and it
# is binary64), `unique(k)` (JSON Schema has no uniqueness-by-property
# keyword), a hidden entry (not generated, so not part of the value a
# consumer produces), a spread on a closed map, and any residue -- an
# unresolved reference is not a property constraint, and guessing one

column1: # DEPRECATION CROSSES AS THE 2020-12 ANNOTATION IT IS. The export used
# to drop the whole record in SILENCE -- no keyword, and no loss line
# even under --strict -- which is the one thing this verb's contract
# says it never does (BUGS.md §56). The flag is faithful; the record's
# STRINGS have no home in 2020-12, so they are a reported loss rather
# than invented into `description` (this exporter emits none, and
# quietly redefining it would be a mapping a consumer cannot undo).

column4: {"lossy":[{"construct":"deprecate","path":"$.a","reason":"JSON Schema 2020-12 has the `deprecated` flag and no field for what it SAYS, so msg cannot cross; the schema marks the property deprecated and a consumer must read the model for the reason"}],"schema":{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","properties":{"a":{"deprecated":true,"minLength":1,"type":"string"}},"required":["a"],"type":"object"},"verdict":"lossy"}

# loss, unless the export is anchored inside a marked block, where the
# marks are the block's own and the export reads through them.
